target.name: CORO1A-DEF6 network (I)
target.description: Centred on coronin-1A and the SLP76-family adaptor DEF6 (IBP/SWAP-70-like), this interaction network describes the actin- and small-GTPase-linked machinery that lymphocytes use to organise their cytoskeleton and secretory traffic after antigen receptor engagement. Coronin-1A regulates F-actin turnover and is required for T cell survival and egress from the thymus; its loss in humans causes a T-lymphopenic combined immunodeficiency, while DEF6 acts as a guanine nucleotide exchange factor toward Rho-family GTPases to shape immune synapse formation and cytokine output.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the myeloid identity and activation program of monocytes and macrophages, the cells that patrol tissue for microbes and debris and set the tone of an inflammatory response. The transcription factor SPI1 (PU.1) specifies this lineage together with HHEX, while TLR4 senses bacterial lipopolysaccharide and PTAFR responds to platelet-activating factor, coupling through the Src-family kinase LYN, the phospholipase PLCB2 and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP (DAP12) to calcium mobilization and cytoskeletal change; DOK2 acts as a brake on this kinase signaling.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on receptor-proximal signalling that converts extracellular cues into changes in cell adhesion, migration and tissue remodelling. target.name: negative regulation of cytokinesis
target.description: Cells must not complete cytoplasmic division until chromosomes are fully cleared from the cleavage plane and the intercellular bridge is ready to be severed, and negative regulation of cytokinesis supplies that restraint. Braking abscission prevents the daughter cells from being cut apart across lagging chromatin, which would otherwise generate DNA damage, aneuploidy and tetraploid or multinucleate progeny.

target.name: Serotonin Neurotransmitter Release Cycle
target.description: Serotonergic signalling depends on packaging serotonin into synaptic vesicles and releasing it in response to an action potential, and this release cycle is the step at which that happens. It supports mood, sleep, appetite and gut motility regulation, and it is the point of action of drugs that block vesicular monoamine loading; loss of release capacity underlies depressive and anxiety states as well as impaired intestinal secretion from enterochromaffin cells.
